title: NHM HMS Challenger sediment/preparation collection: diagnostic object-level harvest and address crosswalk

official_resource.dataset: Listing of HMS Challenger Sediment Collection
official_resource.resource: Sir John Murray's Challenger Sediment Collection

count_states.rule: Preserve all three as dated/documentary catalogue states. The preprint, final article and current live resource are not silently normalized to a single timeless total.

official_resource.resource_metadata_note: The live portal currently describes the resource as XLSX with 4,723 records, while older/localised crawls expose CSV labels. Treat download-format metadata as a versioned portal property rather than a historical collection fact.

preprint_dataset_architecture.core_claim: The preprint describes 4,718 individual items with verbatim label transcription plus details of collection and preparation.
preprint_dataset_architecture.registration_audit: The original Murray M number could represent multiple specimens; the audit allocated bracketed subnumbers to delimit individual items covered by the base M number.
preprint_dataset_architecture.why_it_matters: The current dataset is already a translated address system: legacy group registrations have been decomposed into auditable item addresses without erasing the base historical number.

registration_address_rule.M_prefix: Museum-added Murray Collection registration namespace after transfer into BM(NH)/NHM custody.
registration_address_rule.base_plus_bracket: M base number generally groups material from a sampling site; bracketed subnumber addresses an individual object/preparation within that base record. The current audit can therefore refine, rather than replace, a legacy group address.
non_bijective_examples: M.120 represents material from Challenger Stations 95 and 96.
registration_address_rule.interpretation: Station ↔ M number is a crosswalk, not a guaranteed one-to-one identity.

specialist_return_event.interpretation: The collection includes later specialist working subsets that returned to museum custody; this is not simply an untouched shipboard sediment archive.
specialist_return_event.guard: Published historical reconstruction associates this group with Renard-linked work, but a direct publication-to-each-slide crosswalk remains open.

physical_storage.payoff: A single historical sample can acquire multiple physical and documentary derivatives, so object form must be harvested alongside station and registration address.

row_harvest_limit.problem: The official resource is downloadable but no datastore table/view is exposed on the resource page, and the current binary resource could not be retrieved in this runtime. Therefore this file does not claim a complete 4,723-row spreadsheet harvest.
row_harvest_limit.completed_instead: Object-level records and field architecture explicitly exposed in the official resource documentation and accompanying published/preprint collection study were harvested as a diagnostic layer.
next_when_binary_available: Load every row without early exit.
Subset records whose object/container/preparation wording indicates slide, preparation, thin section, strew, cavity or mounted material.
Search all free-text columns for Haeckel, Norman, Voigt, Hochgesang, Schoep, Renard and other named preparators/annotators.
Preserve M base and bracketed subnumber separately.
Build station → M base → item → preparation-form → specialist → publication fields.

research_payoff: The Challenger material now demonstrates a genuinely non-bijective and historically revised address system. Field station numbers, legacy M registrations and audited preparation subnumbers overlap without collapsing into one namespace. The 4,718 → 4,713 → 4,723 documentary count sequence is itself evidence that collection totals are catalogue states. Named preparations by Haeckel, Norman and Voigt/Hochgesang make the slide cabinet a history of specialist interventions rather than merely a storage residue.
